summary: Rate-window coalescing causing unexpected 429s for small-payload retry waves
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a recurring wave of 429 throttles that appear when a group of small-payload requests (embeds and short chat calls) are retried in tight bursts after transient failures. This is happening in their dedicated pool (us-west) and started after a traffic pattern change last Tuesday. Impact: ~20% of embed calls from their ingestion workers see 429s in short windows; user-facing search latency increases due to retries and backoff amplification. No billing discrepancies reported but customer is concerned about degraded end-user experience. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod-us-west, tenant: orbit-123, ingress fronted by pooled proxy, workers use signed-url uploads and follow-up embed requests. Observed since 2026-03-09 morning spike.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure 50 parallel lightweight workers to perform: a) POST to signed URL (small payload) b) call /v1/embeddings for returned URL (embed-small-v1) 2) Intentionally drop ~10% of initial requests (simulate transient network fail) 3) Let workers retry with client backoff tuned to 100-500ms 4) Observe 429s cluster in short windows and retry amplification. Expected: smoothing or token refill to absorb retries; Actual: multiple small bursts lead to tenant token exhaustion and 429s clustered within same refill epoch.
logs:
Excerpt from gateway logs (2026-03-09T10:12:05Z -> 10:12:20Z):
- 2026-03-09T10:12:05Z INFO request start tenant=orbit-123 route=/v1/embeddings
- 2026-03-09T10:12:06Z WARN transient network error worker=ingest-7
- 2026-03-09T10:12:06Z INFO retry scheduled worker=ingest-7 delay=120ms
- 2026-03-09T10:12:06Z ERROR rate_limiter reject tenant=orbit-123 tokens=0 window_epoch=161792000
- 2026-03-09T10:12:07Z INFO retry fired worker=ingest-7
- 2026-03-09T10:12:07Z ERROR rate_limiter reject tenant=orbit-123 tokens=0
Pattern: rapid retry waves coincide with epoch-aligned refill boundaries and sometimes two proxied connections cause double counting in token accounting.
investigation_notes:
- Verified customer uses short retry backoffs (100-500ms) and high concurrency for small embeds.
- Token refill is aligned on 1s epochs; multiple retries from the same worker push the tenant window to zero within an epoch.
- Observed proxy connection reuse causing duplicate ingress attribution for a subset of requests (edge: pooled-proxy had NAT reuse, resulting in both preflight and actual request being counted).
- Compared metrics vs a control tenant and saw higher token drain rate for Orbit despite similar token budgets.
- No material changes in quota config from customer console in timeframe; they did roll out a worker restart 2026-03-09 09:57 UTC.
- Heap of logs suggests rate-limiter coalescing code groups small requests into the same accounting batch which increases the apparent instantaneous token consumption.
- Correlated with scheduler warmup at the same time which sent healthchecks that were counted against tenant (linked investigation: SUP-412345).
hypothesis:
1) Short backoffs + high concurrency amplify instantaneous token demand vs smooth traffic assumptions, exhausting the per-epoch refill.
2) Ingress proxy double-attribution (preflight + request) for signed URL flows occasionally increments token counter twice for same logical action.
3) Rate-window coalescing behavior (batching accounting checks) doesn't separate background health or preflight calls from user-facing calls, reducing burst headroom.
workaround:
Customer devs implemented: 1) Increase client-side initial backoff jitter to 250-800ms and added exponential backoff cap to avoid tight retry waves. 2) Stagger worker restarts during ingest (5s jitter) to avoid synchronized retry storms. 3) Temporarily disabled a background health probe that was firing per request. Result: 429 frequency dropped by ~70% in the next run.
Support note: Recommend using separate route for healthchecks or request path that is exempt or uses a different background-burst pool (we can propose isolation).
next_steps:
1) Engineering: validate whether ingress-proxy double-attribution bug is present in our pooled proxy (edge) and patch if necessary (assign to Edge team).
2) Product: suggest a conservative default for client-sdks around retry backoff for small-payload embed workflows.
3) Support/SE: propose a rate-pool isolation configuration for Orbit (dedicated) to separate signed-url preflight/health probes from user tokens.
4) Schedule follow-up with customer after edge investigation: target 2026-03-13.
